text:
nina: Heads-up: after the last dashboard perf run we saw auth QPS spike during warmup. thinking about pushing an adaptive preflight that primes permissions for the tenant when a user opens a dashboard; basically warm the permit cache using the dashboard's expected widget permission set.

emil: interesting. how do we build the expected set? static manifest per-dashboard or derive from panel configs at render time?

nina: derive: console can emit a 'required-perms' bundle with the render request. gateway will prime those entries into per-tenant cache asynchronously and the render path will check cache first. the trick is balancing extra work for small dashboards vs big ones.

pavan: op concerns: memory and noisy tenants. we should only prime for dashboards marked as "heavy" or when tenant traffic exceeds threshold. also rate-limit priming per-tenant.

nina: config sketch:

```yaml
priming:
  enabled: true
  heavy_threshold_widgets: 10
  max_prime_per_minute_per_tenant: 5
  prime_async: true
  prime_ttl_ms: 120000
```

nina: integration: console sends header X-Required-Perms: sha256(bundle) and an attachment with list when size small, otherwise store bundle in internal blob store and pass pointer. gateway fetches bundle and schedules priming without blocking render.

emil: metrics: priming_requests_total, primed_keys_count, priming_failures, priming_rate_limit_hits. alerts if priming failures > 0.5%

ops-bot: priming job scheduled in staging cluster.

pavan: rollout plan: dogfood -> opt-in -> canary -> global. include a backoff for tenants that cause high mem churn.

nina: will draft a follow-up RFC today. need reviewers for safety checks.

emil: i'll review the bundle size/serialize format.

nina: thanks all.
